title: JEE Main 2026 (April 2nd, Shift 2) - Mathematics - Matrices and Determinants
subject: Mathematics

questions.q:
If the system of equations
$x + 5y + 6z = 4$,
$2x + 3y + 4z = 7$,
$x + 6y + az = b$
has infinitely many solutions, then the point $(a, b)$ lies on the line:
questions.explain:
For infinitely many solutions, the determinant of coefficients must be zero:
$\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 5 & 6 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 6 & a \end{vmatrix} = 0 \implies -7a + 50 = 0 \implies a = \frac{50}{7}$.
Now using elimination to find $b$, subtracting $R_1$ from $R_3$ gives $y + (a-6)z = b-4$. Subtracting $2R_1$ from $R_2$ gives $-7y - 8z = -1 \implies 7y + 8z = 1$.
For proportional rows: $\frac{1}{7} = \frac{a-6}{8} = \frac{b-4}{1}$.
$b-4 = \frac{1}{7} \implies b = \frac{29}{7}$.
So, $(a, b) = (\frac{50}{7}, \frac{29}{7})$. Checking the options, $a - b = \frac{50}{7} - \frac{29}{7} = \frac{21}{7} = 3$, so it lies on $x - y = 3$.
